 Two teams without a win between them meet at Mendizorroza, and the pressure is real. Deportivo Alavés sit 18th in LaLiga with just 2 points from four matches, while Málaga CF are a place above them on 3 points — close enough that this fixture carries genuine weight for both sides. Neither club can afford to keep watching the table from the wrong end.
 Alavés have the more dangerous attacking unit on paper. Lucas Boyé leads the way with 5 goals and 10 shots on target, and he is backed by a creative engine in Denis Suárez, who has generated 13 chances, and Ángel Hidalgo, who has contributed 3 assists, 5 shots on target, and 9 chances created. That is a lot of firepower for a team that has not won in five matches.
 Málaga bring their own threats. Adrián Niño has scored 3 goals, and Pablo Martínez has been the side’s chief creator with 2 assists and 13 chances created. David Larrubia adds another layer with 4 shots on target and 10 chances created. Málaga’s last outing ended in a 2-5 loss to Real Sociedad, and they need a response.

 Game Preview
 Deportivo Alavés sit 18th in LaLiga with 2 points and a goal differential of -2, while Málaga CF are 16th on 3 points with a -3 goal differential. The gap between them is thin enough that a result here reshapes the bottom of the table in a meaningful way. Both clubs have struggled to find the net consistently, and neither has managed a clean run of form. For Alavés, a home fixture against a fellow struggler is precisely the kind of game they need to convert — dropping points here would deepen an already uncomfortable position.
 What to Watch For
 Lucas Boyé is the player Málaga’s defense must account for above all others. His 5 goals and 10 shots on target make him the most productive attacker in this fixture, and with Ángel Hidalgo creating 9 chances and Mariano Díaz supplying 4 assists behind him, Alavés have the pieces to unlock a Málaga side that conceded five in their last outing.
 For Málaga, the burden of creation falls heavily on Pablo Martínez, whose 13 chances created and 2 assists make him the side’s most influential presence in the final third. Adrián Niño’s 3 goals give Málaga a genuine finisher to target, and if Martínez can find him in space, the visitors have a credible path to their second win of the season.
 What makes this game worth watching is the stakes beneath the surface. Both clubs are fighting to avoid being cut adrift at the bottom of LaLiga. Carlos Dotor adds a goal and 6 chances created from midfield for Málaga, giving them depth in attack. Whoever finds a way to convert their opportunities first is likely to control the outcome.
